# Building an Agentic Engineering Working Stack


You have a machine. It is time to wake it up. 

In this chapter, we build an agentic engineering stack from the bare metal up. We do not rely on hosted platforms that hide the mechanics. You have to understand the rules of the system so you can bend them. We will start with the operating system, load the editor, download the weights, and build the harnesses that turn static code into autonomous operators.

## Starting points

- A minimal personal agent stack can pair a local model such as Ollama or Jan
  with a harness, MCP tools, and memory.
- An always-on personal agent can combine a workspace such as Odysseus or Ajax
  with a messaging gateway such as OpenClaw or Hermes.
- A coding stack can combine OpenHands or OpenCode with repository context
  (DOX) and sandboxed execution.

## Practical considerations

- Incorporate calibrated decision models such as Jev and RLCD for routing,
  gating, and confidence-based escalation.
- Define containment and permission models.
- Understand the cost and token economics of long-running agents.
- Observe and debug multi-step runs.
- Update skills and memory without destabilizing the system.
